source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®; secundum autem, in quo super nubes veniet, superducens diem que est sicut clibanus ardens, et percutiens terram verbo oris sui, et spiritu per labia sua interficiens impios, et ventilabrum in manu habens, et’ emundans aream suam, et triticum quidem in horreum comburens autem paleas igne inexstinguibili. 1. Examrnasir autem et doctrinam Marcionis, quomodo accipiat duos deos esse, infinita distantia separatos ab invicem? Vel quemadmodum bonus erit, qui alienos homines abstrahit ab eo qui fecit, et ad suum advocat regnum? et quare bonitas ejus deficit, non omnes salyans? et quare circa homines quidem bonus videtur, in ipsum autem qui fecit homines injustissimus, auferens ab eo quee sunt ejus? Quomodo autem juste Dominus, si alterius patris exsistit, hujus conditionis que est secundum nos, accipiens panem suum corpus esse confitebatur, et temperamentum calicis suum sanguinem confirmavit? Et quare se Filium Hominis confitebatur, si non eam que ex homine est generationem sustinuisset? Quemadmodum autem et peccata nobis dimittere poterat, quee nostro debeamus factori et Deo? 4Quomodo autem et cum caro non esset, sed cum pareret quasi homo, crucifixus est, et e Jatere ejus puncto sanguis exiit et aqua? Quod autem corpus sepelierunt sepultores? et quid illud erat quod surrexit a mortuis ?
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning was present in all the arrangements of God to men, and announced future things and showed present things and told past things, judges indeed all, but is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the creature more than the Creator, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, nor willing to depart free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law at an unseasonable time, needing nothing from God, and not knowing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, nor willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of his: one indeed, in which he was made man, and suffered weakness, and sat on a foal of an ass, and was rejected as a stone by the builders, and was led as a sheep to sacrifice, and by the extension of his hands dissolved Amalech; but gathering the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and being reminded of his own dead who slept, and descending to them, that he might raise them; but the second, in which he will come upon the clouds, bringing a day which is like a burning furnace, and striking the earth with the word of his mouth, and slaying the impious with the spirit through his lips, and having a winnowing fan in his hand, and purifying his floor, and gathering the wheat into a barn, but burning the chaff with unquenchable fire. But let us examine also the doctrine of Marcion, how he receives that there are two gods, infinitely distant and separated from each other? Or how will he be good, who draws away alien men from him who made them, and calls them to his own kingdom? And why does his goodness fail, not saving all? And why does he seem good towards men, but most unjust towards him who made men, taking away from him what is his? How will the Lord be just, if he exists as the father of another, taking on this condition which is according to us, confessing his bread to be his body, and confirming the mixture of his cup to be his blood? And why did he confess himself to be the Son of Man, if he did not sustain the generation which is from man? How could he also forgive us our sins, which we owe to our maker and God? How could he also, when he was not flesh, but was born as if a man, be crucified, and from his side blood and water flowed out? What was that body which the buriers buried? And what was it that rose from the dead?
pass_b_english: The spiritual disciple is the one who truly receives the Spirit of God. This Spirit was present from the beginning in all God's arrangements with humanity; he announced future events, revealed present realities, and explained the past. He judges all things, yet is himself judged by no one. For he judges the nations—creatures who serve the created order rather than the Creator (Rom 1:25), consuming their entire effort in vain with depraved minds. He also judges the Jews, who failed to perceive the word of liberty and refused to go out free, even though their Liberator was present with them. Instead, they pretended to serve God outside the Law at the wrong time, acting as if He needed nothing, and they refused to know or understand the advent of Christ, which He accomplished for human salvation. All the prophets foretold two advents of His. The first: He became man and knew weakness; He rode on a donkey's colt; He was the stone rejected by the builders; He was led like a sheep to the slaughter; by the stretching out of His hands He overthrew Amalek; He gathered the scattered children from the ends of the earth into the Father's fold; He remembered His own dead who had fallen asleep and descended to them to bring them up. The second: He will come on the clouds, bringing a day that burns like a furnace; He will strike the earth with the word of His mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of His lips; He will hold a winnowing fork in His hand, clear His threshing floor, gather the wheat into His barn, and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire (Isa 11:4; Matt 3:12; 2 Thess 2:8; Mal 4:1).

Now let us examine the teaching of Marcion: how does he accept that there are two gods, separated by infinite distance? How can the one he calls 'good' be good, when he lures away strangers from the God who made them and summons them into his own kingdom? Why does his goodness fail by not saving everyone? Why does he appear good toward human beings, yet prove most unjust toward the One who made them, by stripping that Maker of what belongs to Him? How can the Lord be just if He springs from another Father, yet assumes this human condition, declaring the bread to be His body and the cup's mixture to be His blood? Why did He confess Himself to be the Son of Man if He did not undergo the generation that comes from man? How could He forgive us the sins we owe to our Maker and God? How could He be crucified when He was not flesh, but was born only in appearance as a man—and from His pierced side blood and water flowed out? What was that body the buriers buried? And what was it that rose from the dead?

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and expands upon the scriptural allusions (e.g., Isaiah 11:4, Matthew 3:12, etc.) which are present in the sense of the Latin text, and provides the required inline citations. Pass A is a faithful literal translation. All clauses, including the complex descriptions of the two advents and the Marcionite polemic, are preserved.
